high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. When several things go wrong together, I can panic quickly and feel overwhelmed by what is happening. My feelings may become too much to contain, and tense situations can leave me shaken rather than calm, even when other people regard the pressure as manageable.

I often feel unable to deal with the demands in front of me. Having resources or someone available to help does not always restore my sense that I know how to cope. I may ask for assistance while still feeling helpless about handling the situation myself.

Making up my mind can be difficult. Even when I understand the alternatives and neither choice is dangerous, I can remain stuck between them. When a problem has several interacting pieces, I may struggle to keep them together and feel unable to work out how the parts connect.

Setbacks can leave me knocked off balance for some time. After an unsuccessful attempt or a plan falling through, regaining my footing can be difficult even after the immediate practical trouble is over.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My interests, kindness, ambition, neatness and knowledge can vary independently. I can describe these difficulties coherently; they do not require a clinical diagnosis, a disaster, or a history of failure in every activity.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. When several things go wrong together, I generally remain calm enough to take in what is happening. I can feel disappointed or tense without becoming overwhelmed by my emotions, and pressure usually does not send me into a panic even when the situation matters to me.

I usually feel that I have some way of dealing with the demands in front of me. I can use available resources, seek help when appropriate, and retain a sense that I know how to cope. Needing assistance does not by itself make me feel helpless about the whole situation.

Making up my mind is generally manageable. Once I understand the useful alternatives, I can settle an ordinary choice without remaining stuck between them. I can work through a complex practical problem, keeping its interacting pieces in view and figuring out how they connect.

I tend to recover readily from setbacks. An unsuccessful attempt or a plan falling through can sting, but I usually regain my footing and face what comes next without remaining knocked off balance for long.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My interests, kindness, ambition, neatness and knowledge can vary independently. Calm coping does not require perfect performance, constant happiness, a clinical claim, or success in every activity.
